title: Building an offer that justifies a higher rate for Aquarium maintenance
audience: Aquarium maintenance operators, freshwater and marine, including solo operators, starting or growing a residential, office or retail tank service.
learningOutcomes: Write an aquarium maintenance offer with a clear promised outcome, time frame and conditions
Identify the friction and risk a tank owner carries, and reduce them
Price the offer on value and cost, not only time

instruction.heading: A bad offer versus a good offer
instruction.body: 'I will clean your tank' is a service. 'I will change the water to the schedule we agree, service the filter, test the water and send you the readings with a short note on each visit, and return within the agreed time if a reading falls outside the range we set' is an offer. The owner buys a stable tank they can see, and the certainty that someone is checking it.

instruction.heading: The five parts of an offer
instruction.body: Name the outcome, such as the water change done to the schedule, the filter serviced, and the readings logged. Set the time frame, such as a fortnightly or monthly visit on a stated day. List what the client must do: give access, tell you about new fish or any losses, and tell you before the tank is moved. Give the certainty, which is the readings log and photos. Name the risk you carry, which is the return visit for a reading outside the agreed range. Put the scope and exclusions in writing. Exclusions for an aquarium offer usually include fish rehoming and release, fish-health treatment, the sourcing of marine livestock, and any disposal of tank water beyond the agreed method. A written quote can become binding once it is accepted, so the exclusions protect both sides (business.gov.au, 1 August 2025).

instruction.heading: Reducing friction
instruction.body: Fix the visit day. Put in writing what the client should do with fish during a visit, so they do not decide on the day. Send one readings log that the client can read on a phone. Give one way to pay and one way to change a visit. Fewer steps and fewer decisions for the client usually support a higher price, because the client is paying for convenience and reliability.

instruction.heading: Guarantees and claims
instruction.body: A guarantee must be something you can deliver and afford. Consumer guarantees apply to services, and a 'no refunds' line does not override a customer's rights for services. A written workmanship warranty is an optional promise that sits on top of those rights (business.gov.au, 27 May 2025). Consumer Victoria's guidance says services must be done with due care and skill, but it does not set a fix-window length, so choose a window you can keep and state it. Do not promise fish survival or a water result, because those depend on stock, feeding, equipment and the owner's own actions. Guarantee the visit, the readings and the return visit. Any measured claim needs your own readings behind it.

instruction.heading: Pricing on value
instruction.body: Price from the outcome and the risk, then check the price against cost and time. The only aquarium price found in the research is marketplace data. An Airtasker page for New South Wales shows an average cost range of $105 to $173 per aquarium maintenance expert, with a median of $150, but the unit (per visit, hour or month) is not stated, and the page reports user-posted tasks rather than a price list (last updated 7 November 2026). Do not use it as a visit rate. Good-better-best packages step up in price, with each level adding something the client can see, such as a filter clean or a marine test panel (Jobber Academy, updated 8 October 2024). Show one clear total and say whether GST is included, as the Western Australian guidance asks (WA Consumer Protection, 4 September 2026).

procedure: Write the outcome in one sentence a tank owner would repeat, such as 'a clean filter and logged readings at every visit'.
Set a visit interval you have checked against your own visit records, and record how often you meet it.
List what the client must do, such as telling you about new fish and giving access, and reduce each step.
Add one certainty element: the readings log, the photos and a sign-off.
Decide the return-visit promise and check that you can afford the time it takes.
Price from value, set the price from your own cost, and state whether GST is included.

workedExamples.situation: A Sydney customer wants a freshwater tank drained and cleaned, and its fish rehomed before a move. The tank also holds a marine tank that the customer wants serviced in the same visit. The research found no aquarium price with a stated visit rate.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: Write the offer for the drain and the marine service, and decide what it excludes.
workedExamples.reasoning: The offer names the outcome: the freshwater tank drained and cleaned, the marine tank's water tested and its filter serviced, and a written record of both. It names the client's inputs: a decision on each fish, and access on the day. It excludes the release of any fish into a waterway, because releasing fish into NSW public waters without a permit is illegal (NSW DPI, September 2023). The rehoming arrangement is written down before the visit, and the new home or retailer is named by the client. The marine tank's livestock is not sourced by the business, and the business does not handle marine fish unless it can show that they were lawfully imported. Price is set from the business's own cost and time, not from the marketplace figure.

equipmentAndPpe: Aquarium test kit or digital tester for freshwater and marine readings

commonErrors.error: Guaranteeing fish survival or a water result that depends on stock, feeding or the owner's own actions
commonErrors.prevention: Guarantee only what you control: the visit, the readings, the return visit and your own workmanship.

commonErrors.error: Including the release or unrecorded rehoming of fish in an offer
commonErrors.prevention: Exclude fish release. Write any rehoming arrangement down before the visit, and name the new home or retailer.

commonErrors.error: Quoting a visit rate from a marketplace figure with no stated unit
commonErrors.prevention: Set the price from your own cost and state the basis on the quote.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Business guidance only. This lesson does not grant any licence, registration or authority. No licence requirement for aquarium maintenance was confirmed in any state.

Fish rules are state-based. New South Wales makes it illegal to release fish into public waters without a permit, and to move fish between waterways. Queensland says fish must never be released into waterways, wetlands or drains. Check the rule in each state you work in before any offer includes fish moving.

Marine fish imports are regulated at federal level. The Queensland fact sheet cited in this course says ornamental imports are governed by the federal Live Import List, and that importing or possessing fish imported contrary to the EPBC Act is a Commonwealth offence. That fact sheet dates from June 2020, so check the current federal list before offering any marine livestock service.

qualityStandard: Offer and pricing decisions are written down and checked against cost and time.
Every offer shows its visit interval, what is included, what is excluded, and how each visit is recorded.
documentationEvidence: Written offer or plan, a sample readings log, the evidence collected, and the decision made.
summary: A good aquarium offer promises a stable tank the operator checks, a fixed visit interval, a readings log and a fair return visit.
Higher rates follow from a visible readings log and reliable visits, not from longer hours.

knowledgeChecks.question: Which part of an aquarium offer does the client buy?
options: Your list of tank tools and kit

knowledgeChecks.question: What should a guarantee be?
options: Impossible to claim on in any case
Only for new customers and friends
Something you can deliver and afford

Gap: no per-visit or monthly aquarium maintenance rate from a trade or government source was found. No aquarium trade-body or fish-keeping club source was reached. No marine-specific service rule was found.
